DISTRICT 9 - CGD-GL MSI/General/Miscellaneous

The Coast Guard has transitioned to a visual Maritime Safety Information Products application for the transmission of relevant information previously contained in the published Local Notice to Mariners and Coast Guard Light List. The application, which is accessible at https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/msi, contains the most up to date maritime information overlayed on nautical charts and plotted using latitude and longitude. While the ability to print Local Notice to Mariners and Light List copies is still temporarily available, these printed products lack the positional accuracy of the electronic application and can therefore lead to relevant information being overlooked. Mariners are strongly encouraged to use the Maritime Safety Information Products application as their primary source for all information previously contained in the Local Notic

Location:
Eastern Lake Erie and Buffalo

Due to reduced resource availability, the Coast Guard will be decommissioning the following aids significantly earlier than the advertised Light List date:
Buffalo Harbor North Entrance Channel Lighted Bell Buoy 1 (LLNR 2690).
Buffalo Harbor North Entrance Channel Lighted Buoy 2 (LLNR 2695).
Buffalo Harbor North Entrance Channel Lighted Buoy 4 (LLNR 2700).
Seneca Shoal Lighted Buoy 2 (LLNR 3360).
Early decommissioning is necessary to ensure that the Great Lakes Fall Retrieve Operation is completed prior to the end of the season, and to reduce the possible impacts to waterway restoration in the spring. Any questions or comments can be sent to the Federal Aids to Navigation Manager at the Coast Guard Great Lakes District via email at D09-DG-District-D9-LocalNoticetoMariners@uscg.mil.

MARINE EVENT PERMIT APPLICATION PROCESS MODERNIZATION

The U.S. Coast Guard Navigation Center has launched a new online Marine Event Permit application process effective June 3rd. Marine event sponsors conducting regattas, marine parades, fireworks displays, swim events, or similar activities on navigable waters of the United States are encouraged to utilize the updated online submission capability. Applications should be submitted to the appropriate Captain of the Port at least 135 days prior to the scheduled event.  Marine Event Permit Application and additional information are available at: 

https://navcen.uscg.gov/contact/Application-For-Marine-Event-Permit

Enterprise TE Products Pipeline Company LLC will be conducting excavation, maintenance, and repair operations along an existing natural gas liquids pipeline in the Cayuga / Seneca Canal, located in the Town of Dix, Schuyler County, NY, at approximate position 42°22'03.1"N, 076°51'28.1"W . Operations are scheduled from November 23, 2026, through December 21, 2026.
The active work zone extends 60 feet along the length of the canal and 70 feet out into the canal from the eastern bank. An approximately 160-foot wide navigable channel will remain open for vessel traffic. Work equipment includes an amphibious excavator, an amphibious crane, and up to 10 barges. On-scene equipment will monitor VHF-FM Channel 16. Mariners are advised to exercise extreme caution, maintain a proper lookout, and pass at slow/no-wake speed.
